# **Zamu by OTBLABS: Launch Plan**

Oct 10, 2026 · @Austine Gwa

## **The offer**

Zamu by OTBLABS is an AI receptionist that answers a business's customers on WhatsApp around the clock, books appointments, collects M-Pesa payments and hands over to a person when needed. We sell it as a done-for-you service: we set it up, train it on the client's business and run it for a monthly fee.

**One-line pitch:** Never miss a customer on WhatsApp again, even at 11pm on a Sunday.

**Why it fits OTBLABS:**

* It combines what the team already ships: WhatsApp, M-Pesa Daraja, Zoho and Odoo integration, and AI.  
* It produces monthly recurring revenue, unlike one-off projects.  
* Every client is a warm lead for larger work: CRM setup, ERP automation, custom platforms.  
* It is a live demonstration of the "AI-ready" positioning on the new website.

**Name:** Zamu is Swahili for a shift or a turn on duty. Tagline: "Zamu: always on shift." Check the zamu.co.ke domain and the KIPI trademark register before printing anything. Customers never see the name, because the assistant replies under each client's own business name on WhatsApp.

## **Who to sell to first**

Start with private clinics in Nairobi, then add salons and spas, then private schools. All three already run on WhatsApp, lose money when messages go unanswered, and make a booking or payment that the assistant can complete.

| Segment | Their pain today | What the assistant does | Who signs | Order |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Private clinics, dental and specialist practices | Reception is overwhelmed; after-hours enquiries go to competitors | Answers fees, hours and doctor availability; books and reminds; takes consultation deposits by M-Pesa | Practice owner or practice manager | 1st |
| Salons, spas and barbershops | Bookings arrive by DM and get double-booked or forgotten | Shows open slots, books stylists, takes deposits, sends reminders to cut no-shows | Owner | 2nd |
| Private schools and colleges | Admissions and fee questions flood one phone in January, May and September | Answers admissions FAQs, sends fee structures, shares balances, collects fees by M-Pesa | Bursar or admissions head | 3rd |

Why clinics first: one recovered appointment can cover a month's fee, they already value reminders, and practice managers talk to each other. Property managers and hardware shops are strong later segments once two case studies exist.

## **Version 1 scope**

Version 1 is WhatsApp only, text only, and does five jobs well. Voice calls, more channels and deep ERP links wait until paying clients ask for them.

**In version 1:**

1. Answers questions from the client's own information (services, prices, hours, location, policies) in English and Swahili, and replies naturally to Sheng.  
2. Books, reschedules and cancels appointments against a shared calendar, and sends reminders the day before.  
3. Sends an M-Pesa payment request (STK Push) for deposits or fees, and confirms when it is paid.  
4. Hands the chat to a staff member when the customer asks, when the question is sensitive (medical advice, complaints, refunds), or when it is unsure.  
5. Gives the owner a simple web dashboard: every conversation, bookings, payments and a weekly summary.

**Later, when clients ask:**

* Answering phone calls by voice  
* Instagram and Facebook Messenger  
* Two-way sync with Zoho CRM, Odoo or clinic management systems  
* Outbound campaigns such as promotions and fee reminders to the whole customer list  
* Multi-branch businesses with separate calendars

## **How it is built**

One shared platform serves every client. Each client gets their own WhatsApp number, knowledge base, calendar and M-Pesa till, so a new client is a setup job, not a new build.

**Building blocks:**

* **WhatsApp Cloud API** directly from Meta, so there is no reseller markup. Each client verifies their business in Meta Business Manager and connects their number.  
* **AI model** through an API, answering only from the client's approved information. Start with a small, low-cost model, and send only hard questions to a larger one.  
* **M-Pesa Daraja** STK Push to the client's own till or paybill. Money goes straight to the client; OTBLABS never holds it.  
* **Calendar:** Google Calendar to begin with, since most small clinics and salons already use it.  
* **Dashboard and backend:** Java Spring Boot with Thymeleaf and Tailwind CSS, and a MySQL database, hosted in one place (see the Zamu Software Requirements Specification).

Every client message passes through Meta to the shared platform, which answers, books, requests payment or hands over to staff.

**WhatsApp costs changed on 1 October 2026\.** Meta now charges for replies inside the 24-hour customer window after the first 1,000 per number each month. The Rest of Africa rate is about €0.0033 per message as of 5 October 2026 ([wha.tools](https://wha.tools/whatsapp-api-pricing), [respond.io](https://respond.io/blog/whatsapp-pricing-change-2026)). Kenya most likely falls under that region; confirm on Meta's rate card.

**Estimated running cost per client per month** (to confirm in the pilot):

| Item | Assumption | Approx. KES per month |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| WhatsApp messages | 2,000 replies; 1,000 free, 1,000 at about KES 0.5 | 500 |
| AI model usage | About 600 conversations on a small model | 1,000 to 3,000 |
| Hosting and monitoring share | Shared platform split across clients | 500 to 1,000 |
| **Total** |  | **2,000 to 4,500** |

The euro-to-shilling conversion and AI usage are rough estimates. Track real costs per client from day one.

## **Pricing**

Test a one-off setup fee plus three monthly plans. At the estimated running cost of KES 2,000 to 4,500 per client, the Starter plan leaves a healthy margin and Growth is where most clinics should land. These prices are starting points to test with the first ten prospects, not final.

| Plan | KES per month | Includes | Best for |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Starter | 7,500 | 1 WhatsApp number, up to 500 conversations, FAQs and handover to staff | Small salons, single-doctor practices |
| Growth | 15,000 | Up to 1,500 conversations, bookings and reminders, M-Pesa payments, weekly report | Busy clinics and spas |
| Business | 30,000 | Up to 4,000 conversations, several staff logins, Zoho or Odoo sync, monthly review call | Schools, multi-branch businesses |

**Setup fee:** KES 25,000 for Starter and Growth, quoted separately for Business. It covers Meta business verification, writing the knowledge base, M-Pesa and calendar connection, and staff training.

**Launch offer for the first five clients:** setup waived and the first month at half price, in exchange for a written testimonial and permission to publish results. Ask for a 3-month minimum after the first month.

## **First 90 days**

The goal is ten paying clients by 10 January 2027, in three phases starting Monday 12 October 2026\. Each phase ends with a checkpoint (see the last section) before more time goes in.

**Phase 1: Demo and validate (12 Oct to 1 Nov)**

* ☐ Build a working demo for a fictional Nairobi dental clinic: FAQs, booking and M-Pesa deposit on a test number  
* ☐ Record a 60-second screen video of a customer booking and paying in the chat  
* ☐ List 50 private clinics in two or three areas, such as Westlands, Kilimani and Upper Hill  
* ☐ Visit or call 20 of them. Ask how many WhatsApp messages they get a day and how many go unanswered after hours  
* ☐ Show the demo to the 10 most interested and test the prices

**Phase 2: Pilot (2 Nov to 6 Dec)**

* ☐ Sign five pilot clients on the launch offer  
* ☐ Set each one up within five working days, including Meta verification  
* ☐ Review every pilot's conversations weekly; fix wrong answers and handovers  
* ☐ Measure response time, bookings and payments made through the assistant  
* ☐ Collect a testimonial and one result per pilot, such as bookings taken after hours

**Phase 3: Convert and sell (7 Dec to 10 Jan)**

* ☐ Move pilots to paid plans with a 3-month minimum  
* ☐ Publish two case studies on the website and LinkedIn  
* ☐ Ask each happy client for two referrals to other practice owners  
* ☐ Approach private schools before the January admissions and fee rush  
* ☐ Add a Zamu page to the OTBLABS website with the demo video and a WhatsApp "try it" number

December is slow for many businesses in Kenya. Use it to tighten the product and line up school demos for early January.

## **Competition and how we win**

WhatsApp chatbots are not new in Kenya, so the edge has to be focus and delivery, not the technology. Most existing options are either platforms that businesses must set up themselves, or broad agencies that sell to large companies.

| Competitor | What they offer | Where Zamu is different |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| [HelloDuty](https://helloduty.com/blogs/how-kenyan-businesses-are-using-whatsapp-for-their-businesses) | Kenya-focused WhatsApp API provider with AI agents, M-Pesa Daraja, call centre, SMS and USSD | Broad platform for larger firms; we focus on bookings for clinics and salons, at small-business prices |
| [ChatBots Africa](https://peopledaily.digital/news/chatbots-africa-enables-local-business-to-improve-customer-service) | No-code WhatsApp bot builder with a free plan | Do-it-yourself; we set it up and run it, which busy owners prefer |
| Global tools (Wati, respond.io, SleekFlow) | Shared WhatsApp inbox, automation, priced in dollars | No M-Pesa or Swahili focus; owners must build the bot themselves |
| A second receptionist | A person on the phone and WhatsApp | Works office hours only, costs more, and can't answer ten chats at once |

**How we win:**

1. **Own one niche first.** "The WhatsApp receptionist for Nairobi clinics" is easier to sell and to refer than "AI chatbots".  
2. **Done for you.** Live within five working days, with no setup work for the owner.  
3. **Built for Kenya.** M-Pesa in the chat, Swahili and Sheng, and pricing in shillings.  
4. **Results in the weekly report.** Show bookings and payments the assistant handled, so renewal is easy to justify.

## **Risks and compliance**

The biggest risks are a wrong answer to a patient and mishandled personal data, so both are designed out from the start. Clinics and schools must register with the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC) whatever their size ([Bowmans](https://bowmanslaw.com/insights/kenya-data-protection-getting-ready-for-registration/)). OTBLABS processes their customers' data, so it should register as a data processor too.

| Risk | What could happen | How we handle it |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Wrong or invented answer | The assistant quotes a wrong price or gives medical advice | Answers only from approved content; never gives medical advice; hands over when unsure; weekly review of conversations |
| Health data | Patient details are sensitive personal data under the Data Protection Act, 2019 | Collect only name, phone and appointment reason; signed data processing agreement with each client; access logs; deletion on request |
| Data leaving Kenya | AI and hosting providers store or process data abroad | Choose providers that don't train on customer data; name the transfer countries in the ODPC registration and in client contracts |
| ODPC registration | Operating unregistered as a processor | Register OTBLABS as a data processor; check each client holds its own registration |
| Meta rules | A WhatsApp number is restricted for spam or policy breaches | Reply-first use only; marketing messages only with opt-in; follow Meta's commerce and messaging policies |
| WhatsApp price changes | Meta changes rates again, as it did on 1 October 2026 | Plans are capped by conversations; review margins every quarter |
| Payment errors | A customer pays but the booking is not confirmed | Confirm only on the M-Pesa callback; daily reconciliation report for the client |

Have a lawyer review the data processing agreement and client contract before the first paid client. This plan is not legal advice.

## **What to measure**

Three checkpoints decide whether to keep investing. If a checkpoint misses badly, change the segment or the offer before building more.

| Checkpoint | Date | Go if | Rethink if |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| End of Phase 1 | 1 Nov 2026 | At least 5 of 20 clinics say yes to a pilot | Fewer than 2 say yes: try salons or schools first |
| End of Phase 2 | 6 Dec 2026 | The assistant answers at least 80% of chats without handover, with no serious wrong answers | Most chats need a person: narrow what the assistant handles |
| End of Phase 3 | 10 Jan 2027 | 10 paying clients and at least 4 of 5 pilots renew | Pilots don't renew: interview them, fix the main reason, then sell again |

**Track weekly for every client:**

* Conversations handled and the share handed over to staff  
* Time to first reply, during and after business hours  
* Bookings made and M-Pesa payments collected through the assistant  
* Wrong answers found in the weekly review  
* Running cost per client against the monthly fee

The after-hours bookings figure is the one to put in front of new prospects: it shows money the business would otherwise have lost.
